p: ARMISTEAD MORTALLY WOUNDED. Shot moments after crossing the wall — while touching a Union gun with his hand. Falls beyond the stone wall among Union troops. Armistead asks for Hancock to be brought to him. Hancock also wounded at this moment.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Armistead Mortally Wounded”, Day 3

p: CUSHING KIA. Lieutenant Cushing, serving his last two guns at The Angle, shot through the mouth and killed. Sergeant Fuger assumes command of the shattered battery.

Cowan's Union battery fires canister into Armistead's men at approximately 50 yards — devastating close-range fire. Union infantry closes from multiple directions. The Confederate penetration is contained and then driven back.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Cowan's Union battery fires canister into Armistead's men at approximately 50 yards —…”, Day 3

p: The Confederate penetration is broken. Armistead's men streaming back over the wall or surrendering. Devereux's 19th Massachusetts and others pour into the breach. The Angle is secured.

p.short: Site chronology entry “The Confederate penetration is broken.”, Day 3

p: Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses. Pettigrew's brigades fall back. Trimble (wounded) orders retreat. The survivors stream back toward Seminary Ridge. Lee rides forward to meet them: 'It is all my fault.'

p.short: Site chronology entry “Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses.”, Day 3

p: Lee's acknowledgment — 'It is all my fault' — is one of the most famous statements of the war. He met his broken men personally and attempted to rally them for a Union counterattack that never came.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Along the entire line the Confederate assault collapses.”, Day 3

p: 16TH VERMONT SECOND WHEEL. Stannard's 16th VT wheels again — now against Wilcox's and Lang's Confederate brigades advancing in belated support of Pickett. The double enfilade effectively seals the repulse on the south end.

p.short: Site chronology entry “16TH VERMONT SECOND WHEEL.”, Day 3

p: EAST CAVALRY FIELD. Stuart's cavalry (Hampton, Fitz Lee, Chambliss) attacks east of Gettysburg attempting to reach the Union rear during the main assault. Gregg and Custer's Michigan Brigade block the advance.

p.short: Site chronology entry “East Cavalry Field”, Day 3

p: CUSTER'S CHARGE. Custer personally leads the Michigan Brigade in a mounted charge shouting 'Come on you Wolverines!' The charge stops Stuart's advance. Hampton wounded in melee — sabre cut to head.

Stuart's cavalry repulsed at East Cavalry Field. The Confederate cavalry's last chance to reach the Union rear during Pickett's Charge is gone. Pennington's Union horse artillery fires in support throughout.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Stuart's cavalry repulsed at East Cavalry Field.”, Day 3

p: KILPATRICK'S CHARGE. Kilpatrick orders Farnsworth's cavalry brigade to charge Confederate infantry south of the battlefield. Farnsworth protests: the charge is suicidal over rocky terrain against formed infantry.
FARNSWORTH KIA. Farnsworth leads the doomed charge and is killed — a general for only four days. The charge accomplishes nothing. Kilpatrick's decision is universally condemned.
Meade considers a counterattack. Hancock (wounded) urges one. Meade decides the army is too disorganized and depleted. The counterattack that might have destroyed Lee's army does not happen.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Meade considers a counterattack.”, Day 3

p: Meade's failure to counterattack after Pickett's repulse is his most criticized decision of the battle.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)
p.short: Site chronology commentary on “Meade considers a counterattack.”, Day 3

p: Lee begins organizing his army for defense — expecting Meade's counterattack. When it doesn't come, Lee begins considering withdrawal. Ewell, Hill, and Longstreet ordered to consolidate.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Lee begins organizing his army for defense — expecting Meade's counterattack.”, Day 3

p: Both armies largely stationary. Union troops bury the dead and collect wounded. Confederate artillery conserves remaining ammunition. Lee confers with his corps commanders about the retreat.

p.short: Site chronology entry “Both armies largely stationary.”, Day 3
